A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gen2seg research, with matching architectures, loss equations and core experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation and edge-detection experiments, including Table 1, Figures 5–7 and the appendix loss ablation.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds training-data comparisons, timestep ablations, perturbation tests and decoder-finetuning experiments.

M1.justification: Equation 7 revises the stated prompting rule from inverse feature distance to min(1, inverse feature distance), introducing a cap before normalization. The architectures, generative-model adaptation and three-component instance coloring loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V1 finetunes on Hypersim and Virtual KITTI 2. V2 additionally trains on real-world COCO and synthetic ClevrTex, evaluates five- and ten-class Hypersim supervision regimes, and tests photometrically perturbed COCO images. The original five segmentation evaluation datasets and BSDS500 remain.

E2.justification: SAM, SimpleClick, DINO-B and the Sobel edge baseline remain. However, the separately compared SD-Limited variant disappears from Table 1 and the edge comparison in Figure 6, although it remains in Figure 5. New five- and ten-class variants use different training restrictions rather than simply renaming SD-Limited.

E3.justification: V2 makes AP below 20% recall the main edge summary, replacing v1's full-range AP numbers while retaining full precision–recall curves. Added experiments introduce class-exclusion and image-pruning controls, 15,000-iteration budgets for restricted-category SD models, alternative timesteps, photometric transformations and partial-layer finetuning. These are new experimental settings, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantial analyses of training domain and category diversity (Table 2), timestep sensitivity (Table 5), photometric robustness (Table 6), and the necessary depth of decoder finetuning (Table 7). The original loss ablation survives as Table 4; multi-prompt and background-omission analyses are retained in the appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run error bars. The added experiments continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 42 shared Table 1 values and the original loss-ablation scores are unchanged, but v2 adds extensive results in Tables 2–3 and 5–7 and removes the Table 1 SD-Limited row. V1 Figure 6 reports full-range edge AP of 58.8 for SD and 64.7 for SAM; v2 Table 3 reports 93.4 and 79.0 below 20% recall. This ranking difference reflects different metric coverage, not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Equation 7 changes the mathematical definition of query-feature similarity by adding a non-equivalent cap at 1. The instance definitions and loss formulas in Equations 1–6 remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim that generative pretraining enables transfer to unseen mask categories and styles remains. V2 narrows v1's explicit claims about generalization beyond both pretraining and finetuning distributions to unseen finetuning supervision. Section 3.1 also explicitly disclaims novelty for the finetuning strategy.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations linking clean boundaries to generative priors despite polygonal supervision, locating grouping information in the decoder, and explaining why simple prompting probes representations. It also qualifies the necessary training diversity and interprets perturbation robustness. Existing small-object and background-omission limitations remain. Some new interpretations exceed the evidence: Table 5 shows EgoHOS falling from 40.0 to 28.6 despite describing timestep effects as negligible.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 documents pruning images with over 35% disallowed area or no allowed masks, and the shorter training budgets for restricted-category SD models. Appendix C clarifies previously general data-cleaning descriptions by specifying removal of maskless images and scenes with fewer than ten objects. Core hardware, optimization settings and code-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 replaces the relatively unexplored diffusion-instance-segmentation framing with explicit distinctions from Fan et al. (2024) and Zhao et al. (2025). It adds substantive positioning against pseudo-mask approaches such as FreeSOLO and Cut and Learn, and credits De Brabandere et al. (2017) and Kong and Fowlkes (2018) as antecedents of its finetuning strategy.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around human object generalization and narrow supervision, presenting MAE before Stable Diffusion. V2 removes the standalone qualitative-results subsection, expands the prompting explanation, moves multi-prompt and detailed edge discussion into the appendix, and reorganizes the implementation and ablation sections.

P2.justification: V2 adds five tables, relocates Figures 5–7 to the appendix, and redraws Figure 6 with additional curves and a different legend. Figures 13–19 are substantially reconfigured to display additional training variants. Figure 4 loses one example, Table 1 loses a row, and the title page, headers and document layout change.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central argument by testing dependence on synthetic annotations, category diversity and extensive finetuning (Tables 2–3 and 7), alternative explanations that v1 largely left uncontrolled. It also clarifies the contribution and credits methodological antecedents. Restricted edge AP and unequal training budgets limit some comparisons, and the timestep interpretation is overbroad, but full curves remain available and these drawbacks do not outweigh the substantial added diagnostic evidence.
